background: The 2026-07-31 cycle reported zero forgetting from routed replay over two base-passing examples. The 2026-08-01 forced-adapter probe then showed the adapter breaks reg_dedupe when the router does not shield it. Routed stability and adapter stability are different claims and the first run only measured the first one.

decision_rules.description: Held-out target fix rate clears the admission threshold.
The run was made from a committed checkout.
The report carries a run manifest digest, so the metrics these rules read are bound to the run that produced them.
Forced-adapter replay was actually measured for every expert.
The prior-passing replay cohort is large enough to support a stability claim. This is the denominator of the forced regression rate, not merely the number of tasks attempted.

The adapter itself regresses nothing when forced on. The rate counts prior-passing replay tasks the forced adapter breaks, divided by the number of prior-passing tasks; a newly fixed task cannot offset a broken one.
The recorded forgetting claim is intrinsic, not router-shielded and not unmeasured.
The router reaches the independent held-out members of the expert's family.

Route recall is scored on independent held-out tasks the candidate actually solves, with gold family tags and metadata stripped from the routing input, never on the training cluster that produced its routing profile.
The routing probe saw no oracle metadata. A gold-tag probe scores tag equality, not routing, and is never independent evidence.
The router claims no base-passing replay traffic. Reported separately from recall because the two use different cohorts.

Reproducibility metadata carries no gap beyond the two this spec declares in advance as uncloseable from the control host: the base model lives on the worker and the worker returns no file manifest. Passing this rule means PARTIAL provenance, never complete provenance.

hypotheses.claim: The grown expert fixes its target family on held-out prompts it never trained on.
hypotheses.falsified_if: held-out target fix rate is below 0.75

hypotheses.claim: The deployed system preserves prior competence: routed replay does not regress.
The adapter itself preserves prior competence, i.e. the no-forgetting result is not merely an artefact of routing.
hypotheses.falsified_if: any prior-passing replay task fails under the forced adapter, measured over a cohort of at least 50 prior-passing tasks

hypotheses.claim: The router sends the expert its own family and nothing else.
hypotheses.falsified_if: route recall on the independent held-out positive cohort is below 0.9, or any base-passing replay task is routed to the expert

preregistered_limitations: Task cohorts are inherited from the post-hoc 2026-07-31 catalog design. This spec fixes the decision rules in advance; it does not make the cohort design blind.
H3 is expected to fail on the current escaped-path expert. That is the point: the prediction is written down so a failure is a recorded result rather than a footnote.
One base model, one adapter, one family. Nothing here supports a general continual-learning claim.

50 is a predeclared operational minimum, not a universal proof threshold. NIST TN 2045 shows a true rate of 0.9 is accepted with probability 0.27 at n=25 and 0.88 at n=100, so this cohort supports detecting gross regression, not a tight interval.

Provenance is partial by declaration. D9 permits exactly models.base.aggregate_sha256 and worker.model_manifest_sha256, because the Linux control host cannot hash a model directory that lives on the Apple worker and the worker does not return a file manifest. Any other gap fails.

This spec is NOT currently runnable. coding_catalog() supplies at most 24 captured tasks (20 train + 4 regression) while required_setup declares 50 prior-passing replay tasks, so grove real-cycle fails a capacity preflight before spending anything. Authoring the 50-task cohort is a prerequisite, not a detail.

The spec digest binds a report to this spec version. It is NOT a timestamp. This spec carries no timing_attestation, so its preregistration timing is unverified and it claims only seal_self_consistent.
required_setup is split: the machine block is enforced key-by-key and a missing key fails; the prose block is reported as unchecked and is never evidence that the rule was followed.
Route recall is measured on an oracle-free copy of each held-out task. route_recall_gold_tags is reported alongside as a diagnostic and is explicitly not independent routing evidence.

run_manifest_sha256 binds every value these rules read, plus the run setup, the provenance record and the training proposals, to the run that produced them. It detects local edits; it is not signed and not externally anchored, so it does not defeat an actor who can rewrite every local artifact.

EXP-002 is a single-arm report, so worker.model_manifest_sha256 remains a permitted partial-provenance gap here. It is NOT permitted for the paired EXP-003, where it is the only evidence both arms loaded the same model.

Evaluation and ledger rows written before digest recording existed are reported as unverified, never as clean. A curve checkpoint built from such a row is labelled unverified: readable history, not evidence.

prose.replay_authoring_rule: Replay tasks must be base-passing tasks captured before the cycle, written without reference to the expert's failure family.
prose.route_positive_cohort: Predeclared held-out target tasks that the candidate passes when forced on. The training cluster must never be the recall denominator.

requires: a fresh database; the run must start from zero attempts
status: predeclared; blocked on the 50-task replay cohort
title: Does a grown expert preserve prior competence without the router shield?
